ideas.hypothesis: A policy-rate cut below zero should move 10-year government yields less, and the effect should fade faster, than an equal-sized surprise cut above zero. Pass-through should weaken further as the policy rate nears the lower bound set by cash-storage costs, because long rates depend partly on conventions about where the floor is rather than on real forces alone.

sources.role: method and finding: identification of monetary policy shocks through heteroskedasticity with daily data; at the zero lower bound, effects on long yields die off quickly
mechanism: cash storage costs set a negative effective lower bound; markets adapted to negative rates in Sweden, Denmark, Switzerland and the euro area
mechanism: long-term rates driven by conventions rather than only by loanable-funds fundamentals
mechanism: survey of how negative rates relate to asset prices and the zero lower bound

ideas.test: Daily data for Sweden, Denmark, Switzerland and the euro area, 2009 to 2019: policy rates, 2-year and 10-year government yields, and money-market surprises on policy announcement days. Estimate heteroskedasticity-identified VARs or event-study regressions of 10-year yield changes on policy surprises, interacted with an indicator for a negative policy rate and with the distance to the estimated lower bound. Trace persistence using local projections.
ideas.disconfirming: Long-yield responses to policy surprises are as large and as persistent when the policy rate is negative as when it is positive, or they strengthen near the lower bound.

ideas.hypothesis: In a small New Keynesian model with adaptive learning, letting the effective lower bound fall below zero (into negative rates) should widen the range of policy-rule coefficients under which expectations are stable under learning. It should also shrink the advantage of nominal GDP level targeting over strict price level targeting during lower-bound episodes.

sources.role: method and finding: a small NK model under optimal discretion with a zero lower bound, comparing NGDP level targeting with price level targeting
method: adaptive learning and expectational stability (E-stability) as a criterion for designing monetary policy rules in the NK model
mechanism: the zero lower bound and negative nominal rates as an extension of the policy space
setting: negative (real) rates affecting consumption, saving and investment, informing the model's transmission channels

ideas.test: Calibrate the 3-equation NK model to US or euro-area data. Solve under optimal discretion with the lower bound at 0, -0.5% and -0.75%, and with recursive least-squares learning. Simulate 10,000 episodes with persistent demand shocks and compare welfare losses, the frequency of lower-bound episodes and the E-stability regions across targeting regimes. As an empirical check, compare the dispersion of survey inflation expectations in economies with and without negative rates.
ideas.disconfirming: Lowering the bound does not change the E-stability region or the welfare ranking of the targeting regimes.

ideas.hypothesis: In cost-utility studies that derive QALYs from the SF-36 through the SF-6D, the discount rate should change incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) conclusions substantially for interventions whose benefits are long-lived (such as orthopedic implants) and barely at all for short-horizon ones (such as palliative care). Moving from the conventional 3 to 5% to rates matching the low real yields of the 2010s should flip a meaningful share of reimbursement decisions.

sources.role: method: design of health-economic evaluations alongside implant trials (cost-effectiveness, cost-utility, cost-benefit)
method and measure: SF-6D utilities derived from SF-36 to estimate QALYs for palliative pancreatic cancer care
mechanism: the outcomes movement turns patient-reported scores into objective inputs for decisions
method: systematic review showing that analytic choices for HRQL scores are often inappropriate, which motivates sensitivity analysis

ideas.test: A re-analysis of about 30 published SF-36/SF-6D cost-utility studies with reported cost and QALY streams over time. Recompute ICERs at discount rates of 0%, 1.5%, 3% and 5%, and at the prevailing real 10-year government bond yield in the study country. Count how often the cost-effective verdict changes at a fixed willingness-to-pay threshold, by time horizon.
ideas.disconfirming: ICER verdicts are insensitive to the discount rate across this range, even for long-horizon interventions.

ideas.hypothesis: Survey studies of household interest-rate expectations that use psychometrically validated measures (multi-item or probabilistic bin questions with demonstrated test-retest reliability) should find larger and more precisely estimated revisions in response to monetary policy announcements than designs that use a single unvalidated point-forecast item.

sources.role: mechanism: validation must be adapted to the purpose of evaluative research, with validity weighed alongside other measurement properties
method: a systematic audit of whether the statistical methods applied to questionnaire scores suit them

ideas.test: An online survey experiment with about 2,000 respondents, randomized to a single-item point forecast or a validated probabilistic multi-item module for expected mortgage and deposit rates. Crossed with that, randomize whether respondents are shown a central bank rate announcement. Compare treatment-effect size and standard errors by format, plus 2-week test-retest reliability.
ideas.disconfirming: Estimated responses to the announcement and their precision do not differ between question formats.

ideas.hypothesis: Under co-financed EU Framework Programme funding, a country's sovereign borrowing costs should negatively predict its participation and funding share in transport research projects, beyond what research capacity explains. That would mean EU research money flows away from fiscally stressed members during high-rate periods, which conflicts with distributive-justice principles for allocating research funds.

sources.role: measure and setting: country-level participation, coordination and funding shares in FP6 surface transport projects
mechanism: justice and fairness as ethical criteria for allocating research funds

ideas.test: Country-year panel from CORDIS for FP6 and FP7 transport projects, 2003 to 2013: number of participations, coordinator roles and EU contribution. Merge 10-year sovereign bond spreads over Germany, gross R&D spending (GERD) and researcher headcounts. Regress funding share on lagged spreads with capacity controls and country fixed effects, focusing on the 2010 to 2012 spread surge.
ideas.disconfirming: Sovereign spreads have no association with participation or funding share once research capacity is controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Across the subscales of instruments used in clinical trials, known-groups discriminant validity (how well a subscale separates healthy from ill people at baseline) should not predict responsiveness to the trial intervention (the standardized response mean). The same lack of link should hold for multi-item survey modules used in randomized information experiments on interest-rate expectations.

sources.role: finding and method: Cronbach's alpha is a poor predictor of responsiveness (SRM), from four longitudinal trials
measure: discriminant validity and internal consistency evidence for the WHOQOL-BREF
mechanism: properties needed for evaluative measurement differ from the classic psychometric criteria

ideas.test: Re-analyse 3 to 4 existing longitudinal trial datasets that include the WHOQOL-BREF or SF-36. For each subscale, compute the known-groups effect size at baseline and the SRM after the intervention, then correlate them across subscales. Repeat on a randomized survey experiment that gives households central bank rate information, using its multi-item expectations scale.
ideas.disconfirming: A strong positive correlation (r > 0.5) between discriminant validity and SRM across subscales.

ideas.hypothesis: Subscales with weak convergent validity against an external criterion (for example the SF-36 role-emotional and role-physical subscales against the GHQ-28) should be less responsive in trials and produce more heterogeneous treatment-effect estimates. Likewise, survey scales of household financial stress that correlate weakly with administrative debt-service ratios should respond less to policy-rate increases.

sources.role: finding: SF-36 role subscales show weak convergent validity against the GHQ-28 in elderly Iranians
method: test-retest and validity assessment of paired child and parent instruments
method: SRM as the measure of responsiveness, separate from reliability
mechanism: psychometric methods must be adapted to the needs of evaluative research

ideas.test: Pool 3 or more trials with the SF-36 and a criterion instrument. Compute subscale-criterion correlations and SRMs, and regress SRM on convergent validity with trial fixed effects. As an extension, use a household panel with linked loan data to correlate a financial-stress scale's convergent validity with its change around a policy-rate hike.
ideas.disconfirming: Subscales or scales with weak convergent validity are as responsive as those with strong convergent validity.

ideas.hypothesis: Newly diagnosed breast cancer patients in Medicare managed care should be more likely to disenroll voluntarily to fee-for-service Medicare in counties with many trial sites funded by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) cooperative groups. That pattern would fit patients leaving restricted networks to reach publicly funded trial care, given that trial participation does not raise payer costs.

sources.role: method and data: SEER-Medicare matched comparison of disenrollment from managed care among breast and other cancer patients
finding: trial participation imposes no incremental resource use on a public payer, compared with standard of care

ideas.test: Build a SEER-Medicare cohort of breast cancer patients in managed care, 1995 to 2002, pair-matched to cancer-free enrollees, and merge in county-level counts of NCI cooperative-group trial sites. Estimate a Cox model of time to disenrollment, with an interaction between cancer diagnosis and trial-site density.
ideas.disconfirming: Excess disenrollment among breast cancer patients does not rise with local trial-site density.

ideas.hypothesis: As with prostate cancer, enrolling colorectal cancer patients in clinical trials should impose no significant incremental one-year cost on a public payer compared with standard-of-care treatment. If so, the perception of trials as a cost burden should not be used to argue against funding them.

sources.role: method and finding: a matched retrospective cohort with standardized price templates finds no cost difference for prostate cancer trials
setting: colorectal cancer patients as a large group whose payer and coverage choices affect costs

ideas.test: A retrospective matched cohort at one cancer centre: about 60 colorectal cancer patients in industry or cooperative-group trials and 60 eligible non-participants receiving standard of care. Track one year of resource use (visits, imaging, chemotherapy, admissions) and cost it with standardized public-payer price templates. Run a two-sided test of the mean difference, and a sensitivity analysis by trial sponsor.
ideas.disconfirming: Trial participants incur significantly higher public-payer costs than matched standard-of-care patients.

ideas.hypothesis: In BRIC countries, faster diffusion of personal computers and the internet, which is driven more by tertiary enrollment than by the cost of credit (real lending rates), should come before the institutionalization of research ethics oversight for emerging converging technologies (registered ethics committees, national ethics guidelines for NBIC research).

sources.role: finding and measure: links between educational attainment and the diffusion of ICT indicators (internet users, personal computers) in Brazil, China and India
setting: BRIC innovation policy for converging (NBIC) technologies and the governance questions they raise

ideas.test: Country-year panel for Brazil, Russia, India and China, 1995 to 2018: personal computers per 100 people, internet users, tertiary enrollment, real lending rate (World Bank World Development Indicators), and a hand-coded index of research ethics institutions (number of registered ethics committees, dates of national guidelines). Run Granger-type panel regressions of the ethics index on lagged ICT diffusion, controlling for R&D spending.
ideas.disconfirming: ICT diffusion does not predict later development of ethics institutions, or real lending rates explain PC diffusion better than education does.
